evidence_items.locator: Section 'Early returns on GenAI', paragraph following the reported efficiency, revenue, and profitability results
evidence_items.explanation: PwC reports employee-time efficiencies for 56% of CEOs, revenue increases for 32%, and profitability increases for 34%, with results below earlier expectations. This offers qualified support for benefits remaining elusive in numerous settings, but does not count failed applications or establish the investment total.

evidence_items.locator: Section 'Scaling is still a work in progress — some uses are outpacing others'
evidence_items.explanation: The July–September 2024 survey reports positive returns for organizations' most advanced scaled initiatives. This materially limits a broad failure narrative, but successful selected initiatives do not disprove difficulties in many other applications.

evidence_items.publisher: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.explanation: The report estimates global private generative AI investment at US$33.9 billion in 2024. This annual funding measure neither verifies nor refutes a cumulative total that may include infrastructure spending; treating it as a direct contradiction would change the metric.

unresolved_gaps: No transparent, comparable calculation establishes approximately US$500 billion of accumulated generative AI investment by publication.
The investment claim has no stated accounting basis or boundary between financing and spending.
The surveys measure organizations and selected initiatives, not a representative count of application-level successes and failures.
Missing financial gains do not necessarily mean an application missed its intended operational goals.
